questions.stem: The schematic shows the paired embryonic aortic arches connecting the aortic sac to the dorsal aortae. Which of these arches normally persists to form the definitive arch of the aorta in the adult?

explanation.summary: Of the six paired aortic arches, the left fourth arch persists as the arch of the aorta; the left sixth forms the ductus arteriosus, the third arches contribute to the carotid system, and the first, second, and fifth largely regress.
explanation.whyCorrect: Of the six paired aortic arches, the left fourth arch persists as the arch of the aorta; the left sixth forms the ductus arteriosus, the third arches contribute to the carotid system, and the first, second, and fifth largely regress.

questions.stem: In this dissection view of the great vessels and neck, the right recurrent laryngeal nerve is labeled. Around which structure does this nerve hook on the right side?

explanation.summary: The right recurrent laryngeal nerve loops beneath and around the right subclavian artery before ascending to the larynx, whereas the left recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks around the arch of the aorta near the ligamentum arteriosum.
explanation.whyCorrect: The right recurrent laryngeal nerve loops beneath and around the right subclavian artery before ascending to the larynx, whereas the left recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks around the arch of the aorta near the ligamentum arteriosum.

questions.stem: This rhythm strip shows QRS complexes that alternate in amplitude from one beat to the next in a patient with a large pericardial effusion. What is the underlying cause of this finding?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Alternating conduction block within the AV node

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bundle branch block that alternates between beats

choices.label: D
choices.text: Swinging motion of the heart within the fluid-filled pericardial sac

explanation.summary: Electrical alternans is produced by the beat-to-beat 'swinging' of the heart as it moves back and forth within a large effusion, changing the QRS vector relative to the ECG electrodes. It is seen in a minority of tamponade patients and, with low-voltage QRS, suggests a large effusion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Electrical alternans is produced by the beat-to-beat 'swinging' of the heart as it moves back and forth within a large effusion, changing the QRS vector relative to the ECG electrodes. It is seen in a minority of tamponade patients and, with low-voltage QRS, suggests a large effusion.

questions.stem: This schematic and paired echocardiogram demonstrate inward buckling of the right ventricular free wall during diastole. This early sign is most specific for which condition?

explanation.summary: Diastolic collapse of the low-pressure right ventricular free wall indicates that intrapericardial pressure is transiently exceeding RV filling pressure, an early echocardiographic sign of cardiac tamponade. The right-sided chambers collapse first because they operate at the lowest pressures.
explanation.whyCorrect: Diastolic collapse of the low-pressure right ventricular free wall indicates that intrapericardial pressure is transiently exceeding RV filling pressure, an early echocardiographic sign of cardiac tamponade. The right-sided chambers collapse first because they operate at the lowest pressures.

questions.stem: This illustration shows a needle being advanced beneath the xiphoid toward the heart to aspirate fluid from around it. What is the name of this emergent procedure used to treat cardiac tamponade?

explanation.summary: Pericardiocentesis is percutaneous needle aspiration of fluid from the pericardial space, typically via a subxiphoid approach with a 16-18 gauge needle. It is the treatment of choice for relieving hemodynamic compromise in cardiac tamponade.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pericardiocentesis is percutaneous needle aspiration of fluid from the pericardial space, typically via a subxiphoid approach with a 16-18 gauge needle. It is the treatment of choice for relieving hemodynamic compromise in cardiac tamponade.

questions.stem: This echocardiogram and accompanying schematic demonstrate collapse of the right ventricular free wall during ventricular diastole in cardiac tamponade. Why is this chamber affected earliest?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is the last chamber to contract in the cardiac cycle

choices.label: B
choices.text: It lies farthest from the pericardial surface

choices.label: C
choices.text: It has the thickest myocardial wall of the four chambers

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a low-pressure chamber, so rising intrapericardial pressure exceeds its filling pressure first

choices.label: E
choices.text: It generates the highest systolic pressure in the heart

explanation.summary: As intrapericardial pressure rises it first overcomes the pressure in the lowest-pressure chamber. The right ventricle fills at low diastolic pressures, so its free wall collapses in diastole before the higher-pressure left-sided chambers, making this an early echocardiographic sign of tamponade.
explanation.whyCorrect: As intrapericardial pressure rises it first overcomes the pressure in the lowest-pressure chamber. The right ventricle fills at low diastolic pressures, so its free wall collapses in diastole before the higher-pressure left-sided chambers, making this an early echocardiographic sign of tamponade.

questions.stem: This illustration shows a needle being advanced at roughly 45 degrees below the xiphoid toward the sac surrounding the heart. What is the purpose of the procedure depicted?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aspiration of fluid from the pericardial space to relieve tamponade

choices.label: B
choices.text: Biopsy of the myocardium for suspected myocarditis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Placement of a transvenous pacemaker lead

choices.label: E
choices.text: Intracoronary injection of a thrombolytic agent

explanation.summary: The image depicts pericardiocentesis: percutaneous needle aspiration of pericardial fluid via a subxiphoid approach angled toward the pericardial sac. It is the emergent treatment for cardiac tamponade, removing fluid to restore diastolic filling.
explanation.whyCorrect: The image depicts pericardiocentesis: percutaneous needle aspiration of pericardial fluid via a subxiphoid approach angled toward the pericardial sac. It is the emergent treatment for cardiac tamponade, removing fluid to restore diastolic filling.

questions.stem: This diagram contrasts a normal heart (left) with a heart in cardiac tamponade (right). What is the primary mechanism by which the accumulated pericardial fluid reduces cardiac output?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It causes acute mitral and tricuspid valve regurgitation

choices.label: B
choices.text: It increases left ventricular afterload via systemic vasoconstriction

choices.label: C
choices.text: It directly reduces myocardial contractility through ischemia

choices.label: D
choices.text: It compresses the chambers and impairs their diastolic filling

choices.label: E
choices.text: It occludes the epicardial coronary arteries

explanation.summary: The illustration shows pericardial fluid compressing the low-pressure right heart chambers, reducing the space available for diastolic filling. Decreased filling lowers stroke volume and cardiac output, which is the central hemodynamic mechanism of tamponade.
explanation.whyCorrect: The illustration shows pericardial fluid compressing the low-pressure right heart chambers, reducing the space available for diastolic filling. Decreased filling lowers stroke volume and cardiac output, which is the central hemodynamic mechanism of tamponade.

questions.stem: The illustration contrasts a normal heart with the heart on the right. What mechanism most directly explains the reduced cardiac output in the condition shown on the right?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Loss of ventricular contractile force from ischemic myocardium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Backward leakage of blood through an incompetent mitral valve

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rapid ventricular rate preventing adequate coronary perfusion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fixed narrowing of the aortic outflow tract raising afterload

choices.label: E
choices.text: External pericardial fluid compresses the chambers and limits diastolic filling

explanation.summary: The right panel depicts cardiac tamponade: accumulated pericardial fluid raises intrapericardial pressure and compresses the right-sided chambers, reducing venous return and diastolic filling, which lowers stroke volume and cardiac output.
explanation.whyCorrect: The right panel depicts cardiac tamponade: accumulated pericardial fluid raises intrapericardial pressure and compresses the right-sided chambers, reducing venous return and diastolic filling, which lowers stroke volume and cardiac output.
